newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek authorities board ship with illegal aliens.
newsitem.headline: Greek authorities board ship with illegal aliens.

text.p: A Ukrainian-registered ship carrying some 200 illegal immigrants was being towed to port by the coastguard on Wednesday after suffering a power failure in the Aegean Sea, the Merchant Marine Ministry said.
"Coastguard officials are now aboard the ship, interviewing the crew and some of the passengers, which include women and children," a ministry official told Reuters.
The spokesman had no details of the origin of the ship and the nationality of the immigrants.
He said tugboats were towing the motorship Sohol, which had been spotted at dawn drifting off the island of Andros, off the coast near Athens.

The immigrants had lit fires in barrels on the ship to get help, the spokesman said. Greek television showed scores of dishevelled people on deck, waving their arms and pieces of white cloth like flags at helicopters hovering above them.
Officials said the Sohol's captain, contacted by radio, had told them he was carrying milk and rice to Italy.

Thousands of illegal immigrants are smuggled into Greece every year from the Third World, most paying thousands of dollars in passage fees. Many come by sea from Turkey and others cross Greece's rugged northern borders illegally.
Greek patrol boats ofter intercept Turkish boats, bringing mostly Iraqis and Kurds to Greek islands.

The extent of the illegal immigrant trade in the Mediterranean was made apparent last January after about 300 would-be immigrants were believed to have perished in a collision between smuggling boats off the coast of Sicily on Christmas Day.
The accident came to light after survivors smuggled into Greece told their story to the police.
